newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products - IPE gas oil delivery seen small.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products - IPE gas oil delivery seen small.

text.p: NWE oil products were mixed on Thursday, gas oil falling, fuel oil rising and mogas simply widening its price range further, dealers said.

Heating oil barges were down by around $1 a tonne as IPE gas oil futures fell. The expiration of June futures at 1100 GMT today ensured physical trading was at a minimum, although sellers re-positioned their offers, now related to the July futures contract, to +50 cents.
Traders said the delivery volume against expired IPE June futures was likely to be very small. The average of estimates was around 50,000 tonnes.

However, sizeable exchanges for physical (EFP) deals were likely to have lifted the effective delivery amount to 200,000-250,000 tonnes, dealers said. One trading house, last month's recipient, was seen as the exclusive deliverer this month, all out of Antwerp.

Gasoline barge prices varied widely, but the underlying trend was unchanged. Two parties concluded their now standard fob AR morning deal for the fourth consecutive day. Today's price, $187 fob AR, was as on Wednesday.

Talk for Rotterdam running refinery material, however, was almost $10 a tonne above the fob AR levels. One trading house was keen to pick up material very promptly, bidding at $195 fob. The offer came at $197.

Fuel oil barges initially traded at $83 fob Rotterdam, but swiftly rose to the range $85-$86 fob, with a number of deals concluded. Late morning offers were at $86, but were seen likely to edge higher.
Some traders said Rotterdam material was in short supply, but bunker demand was unexceptional.
